concerns.text: Tasks T028-T034 implement metrics (SelfPredictionPenalty, BehavioralAdaptationScore, ComputationalIrreducibilityCheck, etc.) that are entirely absent from spec.md and plan.md. This constitutes scope creep and violates the constraint that every task must trace to a defined FR/SC. The spec explicitly limits operationalization to 'self-consistency, calibration, error detection' (Assumptions).

Task T012 mandates a confidence-prediction loss using 'internal generation' (self-consistency proxy). However, plan.md (Complexity Tracking) explicitly mandates 'pre-computed teacher labels' (external truth) to break tautology. The task silently overrides the plan's architectural decision without a spec amendment, creating a semantic conflict with the approved implementation strategy.

Task T032 requires comparing output against a 'pre-computed lookup table of the first N steps' for an Irreducibility Check. Neither spec.md nor plan.md defines this lookup table, its generation method, or its size. This task requires inventing a new artifact and methodology not authorized by the spec, violating the Single Source of Truth principle.

Task T031 requires reporting 'SelfModelOverhead' (tokens, time, memory) as a specific metric. The spec's Success Criteria (SC-001 to SC-005) and Functional Requirements (FR-001 to FR-007) do not mandate computational cost reporting. This is a silent relaxation of the scope to include 'gold-plating' metrics not required by the research question.

Task T029 implements 'BehavioralAdaptationScore' to measure improvement when 'explicitly instructed' to use self-models. The spec's FR-003 and US-02 define evaluation strictly as 'generate 10 reasoning paths' with fixed parameters. Introducing 'explicit instruction' prompts alters the evaluation protocol defined in the spec without a corresponding FR amendment.
